Assessment with SLOOS overlay:
- Fed statement: Growth and employment strengthening; inflation elevated; risks from COVID variants. Policy normalizes via a faster taper while holding the policy rate at 0–0.25%, keeping overall conditions accommodative.
- SLOOS signals: Banks broadly eased standards across residential real estate (including mortgage categories and HELOCs), CRE (multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential), and consumer credit (credit card, auto). Banks increased credit limits on cards and reduced auto loan rates. Demand strengthened for consumer loans and banks expect stronger demand for credit cards and C&I ahead, though some reported near-term softness in C&I and auto demand. Foreign banks eased CRE standards with stronger CRE demand, while C&I demand at foreign banks was mixed.
- Implications: Easier bank credit supply and improving demand point to supportive credit conditions that reinforce the recovery and could accelerate loan growth, offsetting some macro risks. This tilts the tone modestly more positive than the statement-plus-FSR read, even as elevated inflation and market-sensitivity risks remain.

Net read: Balanced-to-positive, with SLOOS indicating accommodative credit that supports growth and narrows downside risk.
